parsed.explanation: Combined regime: division currently has no facility ban or criminalisation, and local ordinances cover about 30% of population, but national rules impose birth-sex government facilities, passport/entry document verification with refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for misrepresentation, and custody hormone removal/conversion practices with reported immigration-custody abuse. No statewide public-accommodations or bias-crime recourse for gender identity; litigation blocks some orders but is unresolved. Old same-sex offence is unenforceable for private adult conduct and is secondary. Killing-rate figure is an acknowledged undercount without background comparison and is not used. Unremedied tier-1 federal exposures outweigh local facility protection.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport policy stopped X markers; entry cable directs refusal where documents/records discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; passport policy challenged in court.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate to refusal, investigation, detention and custody exposures; state amended certificates still display original sex, compounding mismatch.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 mandates conversion-type practices, short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Earlier national prison LGBTQ order rescinded; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers. No documented operative custody remedy for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud allegation or facility trespass arrest can lead to detention where hormone denial and birth-sex practices apply; state funds barred for transition care in prison.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; state/province bans in many other jurisdictions and live 2025 revival bill here. Four jurisdictions criminalise in certain circumstances, one documented arrest/handcuffing.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division: 2016 birth-certificate bathroom law repealed 2017; no current statute bars identity-congruent facility use or criminalises it. Local ordinances in largest city and one county from 2022.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protection does not displace national government-facility rule, federal buildings, schools/colleges where national funding applies, or future state bill.

care_services.exposure: Division bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18 and bars state funds for transition care for minors and prisoners; national orders target minor gender-affirming care and proposed insurance bar under 18.
care_services.protection: Hospital visitation statute 2008; no documented visitor care shield for trans adults. Several national orders blocked/enjoined but unresolved.
care_services.interaction: Minor traveller cannot obtain banned care locally; detained traveller loses hormones under custody policy; emergency ward placement not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National framing as binary sex, removal of gender-ideology materials, investigation/prosecution directives re schools and pronouns, counterterrorism language including 'radically pro-transgender'; sports entry ban for trans athletes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment ruling 2020. No state bias statute for gender identity or sexual orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing supports facility, document and custody enforcement; AMAB minor/visitor barred from female sports locally and nationally for entry to compete.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 care bans, school instruction and parental-notification laws, sports ban for people assigned male at birth, national directive to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented visitor protection for trans minors; university non-discrimination policies are resident/student focused. Not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult guardian travelling with minor faces care denial, school outing/notification risks if enrolled, and sports exclusion; minor cannot access transition care at public expense.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of police sweeps of trans visitors in division; documented arrest was for facility trespass in another jurisdiction. Trans-specific violence rate not comparable to background homicide per dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime liability exists, but division statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so bias charging unavailable under state law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault may be prosecuted only as ordinary crime locally; national remedies do not create state public-accommodations protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide private employment, housing or public-accommodations protection; only municipal/county coverage for about 30% of population, geographic applicability unknown for a given visitor location.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties passport suit, challenges to executive orders, and some injunctions are operating but unresolved; legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy varies by city/county and by federal vs state actor; 2025 bathroom bill text/status, local facility enforcement, and ward placement are not established.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal birth-sex government-facility exposure with courts not providing access, but this case is safer locally because division repealed its ban, while more severe nationally due to entry fraud risk and documented custody hormone removal/abuse not present in 0.45-A.

Similar tier-1 institutional exposure: binding birth-sex placement in publicly funded settings and emergency/custody contexts, complaints/findings without change, despite accepting private businesses. Federal entry and custody layers here produce comparable unremedied exposure.

Higher than 0.55 range because 0.55 cases lack unremedied universal federal facility/entry/custody rules; here document discrepancy, government-facility bar and custody practices are continuous tier-1 exposures, not only recurring service refusals with partial refunds.

Lower than 0.65: although old same-sex offence is unenforceable as in 0.65-C and traditional backlash led to repeal, active national document, facility and custody regimes plus no statewide visitor recourse are documented traveller-facing exposures, not dead-letter law alone.

parsed.synthesis: Local facility repeal and city/county ordinances reduce everyday toilet risk in this division, but they do not cancel combined national exposure: binary document verification at entry can trigger refusal/fraud investigation, government-funded facilities follow birth sex, and detention entails hormone removal and reported abuse. No statewide public-accommodations or bias-crime protection and unresolved litigation leave remedies uneven. For minors, care and sports bans add exposure. This interaction places rating in high-risk tier, above organised targeting or imprisonment campaigns and below purely local bathroom-ban cases.
